data.title: Rome's Long Decline
sentences: Rome’s fall was a slow erosion that reshaped Europe.
It began in 235 CE when Maximinus Thrax seized power.
Civil wars and invasions destabilized the empire until 260 CE.
Valerian’s capture by the Sassanids in 260 CE shattered Rome’s prestige.
Diocletian introduced the Tetrarchy, reformed taxes, and reorganized the army.
In 285 CE he split the empire into East and West.
Diocletian abdicated in 305 CE; Constantine became sole ruler.
Constantine’s 312 CE victory at Milvian Bridge led to Christian conversion.
He founded Constantinople in 330 CE, shifting power eastward.
Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus in 476 CE, ending the Western Empire.
The Eastern Roman Empire persisted until 1453 CE, preserving law and culture.
